## About
Dennis Wells Machine Shop is home to Wells Racing Engines. Dennis has spent his career building performance engines for circle track, drag racing, boats and the street, and many of the folks working alongside him have been here for more than a decade.
The goal is to do all of the work in house. That covers cylinder heads, blocks, crankshafts, rods, pistons, intakes, oil pumps, fuel injection and plenty of smaller jobs. Dennis and Sharon Wells own and run the shop, and David Schweizer handles cylinder heads and customer service.
Customers give the shop a 4.8 rating from 85 Google reviews, and a lot of them mention fair pricing and a team that takes time to explain the work.

## Services
- Cylinder head work: Rebuilding cylinder heads, including after a timing belt failure.
- Head porting and polishing: Porting and polishing work on cylinder heads, handled by the shop's head department.
- Block and rotating assembly: Balancing the full rotating assembly, plus decking and honing the block.
- Freeze plugs, cam bearings and studs: Installing new freeze plugs and cam bearings, balancing, and installing ARP main and rod studs.
- Fuel injection nozzle work: Ultrasonic cleaning, flow testing and spray pattern inspection for injection nozzles.

## FAQ
Q: Where is the shop?
A: We're in Duncanville, one block west of Highway 67.

Q: How much does a job cost?
A: Prices can change depending on how difficult the work is, and many jobs are priced by phone. Give us a call for a quote.

Q: How fast will you answer my email?
A: We read messages every afternoon, but it can sometimes take a couple days to reply. If you need help right away, call the shop.
